frames.narration: Offline: 7 help pages are split into 30 word chunks (10 chunks, no overlap). Each chunk is stored with its text, keyword postings, an embedding vector, its page id, and who may read it.

A customer asks: how long can I send back a laptop after delivery? The query is rewritten into search terms: the stop words go, and a real system may also add 'return' and 'days'. Rewrite is off in this run.

states.retriever: terms: long, send, back, laptop, delivery

frames.narration: The retriever asks the index for candidates by keyword and by vector similarity, then merges the two ranked lists. This toy scores term overlap weighted by idf. Top 3: warranty#0 (135), shipping#0 (76), returns#0 (53). The chunk holding the laptop sentence, returns#1 (51), is 4th.
Context assembly: the 3 chunks cost 135 tokens, well inside the 240 token budget, so all of them are packed with their citation tags. Nothing was cut, but the right chunk was never selected.
The prompt goes to the model with an instruction to answer only from the sources and to cite them. The sources are shipping, warranty, and the accessories paragraph of the returns page.

The model finds '14 days of delivery' in returns#0 and answers 14 days with a citation. It followed the rules and is wrong: that line is about accessories. The failure is in retrieval, so a bigger model will not fix it.

Fix: re-chunk with 10 words of overlap (still 10 chunks). Now returns#1 starts earlier and carries the full sentence, and it scores 77, second behind warranty#0 (133). Reranking the top candidates would also help.
The prompt is still 135 tokens. The model answers: 30 days from delivery, if the laptop works and has its packaging, citing returns#1. The user can open the source and check it.
Freshness and safety live here too: when the policy page changes, only its chunks are re-embedded and the old ones deleted, and every query filters by what this user may read before ranking.

states.index: re-index page, ACL filter at query
